issues.problem: ASCII ' and " after a figure are feet/inches (or arc-minutes/seconds) units, but the tokenizer drops them as quotation marks, so a claim that changes or removes the unit is 'supported'. Same class as the r8 unit-case blocker (5 MB/5 Mb).

issues.problem: '!' is dropped everywhere, so the operator '!=' becomes '=' and a claim that inverts a condition is 'supported' (also 5! vs 5).
issues.evidence: 'The flag x = 0 is set.' <= 'The flag x != 0 is set.' supported; 'Set x = 0 in config.' <= 'Set `x != 0` in config.' supported; end to end /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H8a9-probe/runs/e-neq ('Requests with status = 200 are retried.' <= 'Requests with status != 200 are retried.'): --strict pass, exit 0, supported. 'The result is 5.' <= 'The result is 5!' supported. (Pre-existing.)
issues.suggested_fix: Drop '!' only as sentence punctuation (followed by whitespace, a closing quote/bracket or end of text); otherwise keep it as a token, so '!=' and '5!' survive.

issues.problem: Only 'No,' and 'No.' are exempted. An interjection 'No' followed by ':' ';' '…' or a closing quote, and the abbreviation 'No 1', are still negators, so honest claims are contradicted and --strict exits 1. Incomplete fix of r8-M2.

issues.suggested_fix: Treat 'no' as a negator only when the raw text after it is whitespace followed by a letter (not punctuation, a closing quote or a figure). Add these pairs to the honest corpus.

issues.problem: Accounting notation '(5.3)' means -5.3, but parentheses are dropped, so a sign flip is 'supported'.
issues.evidence: 'Net income was 5.3 million.' <= 'Net income was (5.3) million.' supported. ('$(5.3)' vs '$5.3' is correctly needs_review.) Pre-existing.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep '(' and ')' as tokens when they enclose exactly one figure (regex '\(\s*<figure>\s*\)' -> one token '(5.3)').

issues.problem: Ratio/time colon dropped: '3:1' equals '3 1', '1:10' equals '1, 10'. The resulting claims are odd text, so low risk.
issues.evidence: attack9.py rows 'ratio colon vs space' and 'ratio colon vs comma' supported.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep ':' between two digits as part of the figure ('3:1', '10:30').

issues.problem: Doc says 'the code has no others' but omits that a space after a currency symbol is ignored ('£ 5m' = '£5m') and that ’/ʼ are read as '. The module docstring's allowed list omits contractions and citation markers. 'a plural is a different word' starts a sentence in lowercase.
issues.evidence: attack8.out: 'Acme raised £ 5m.' <= 'Acme raised £5m.' supported; QUOTE_MARKS maps U+2018/2019/02BC.
issues.suggested_fix: List both in quality-gates.md and the docstring.

issues.problem: Residual, allowed by the binding rule: the first word's capital alone may differ, so 'Polish/polish', 'May/may', 'Turkey/turkey' at sentence start match when a quote starts in lowercase.
issues.evidence: attack9.py 'cap polish/Polish', 'cap may/May' supported (quote starting lowercase). Mid-sentence case is exact.
issues.suggested_fix: Accept as documented residual risk, or fold the first word only when the quote's first word is capitalised and the claim's is lowercase.

aggregation: ANY-supports / EVERY-contradicts matches docs. An identical quote makes the claim supported by construction (the sentence is in the cited evidence); an irrelevant non-identical quote cannot raise a verdict to supported. With quotes ['rose','fell'] the claim 'fell' is supported because 'fell' is quoted: inherent to whole-quote matching, quote provenance is not verified here. Empty quotes never support; an empty quote alone vs a one-word negator claim ('Not.') gives contradicted (degenerate, harmless).
